summary: The corrected harness executed in the clean copy and the retained receipt answers the question. Both declared comparisons hold: comparison 0 (within-capacity restart returns) evaluated result indices 1, 3, 7, 13, and comparison 1 (over-capacity restart does not return) evaluated 5, 9, 11; each result was correlated to its own pre-restart prefix event by case identity, with no missing, contradictory or outside-applicability observations and no parse errors. The boundary is pinned: 8189 FSM-bound window entries -> 128 batches -> returns in 4ms, while 8196 entries -> 129 batches -> does not return; the MaxAppendEntries=4 case (same ~1000-entry window, 250 batches) blocks while the 64-entry-batch equivalent returns in 0ms, isolating the batch-size factor, and the post-snapshot case applies the same 12000 commands to the same stores yet returns in 7ms because the window drops to 0. Every non-return sampled a goroutine still inside the replay send, with frames at raft.go:1305 (the batch select-send in processLogs), raft.go:1346, api.go:753 (restoreFromCommittedLogs) and api.go:606 (NewRaft) — the send whose only reader starts later at api.go:637. The appended interpretation therefore moves the finding from a source-only conditional account to a retained, execution-grounded one (conclusion holds, defect claim asserted), reusing the two knowledge entries with their exact revisions, and it keeps the honest counterevidence (opt-in flag, the unreachable shutdown arm, probe-constructed windows) and limits (single-voter in-memory setup, batch sizes only 4 and 64, unmeasured queue memory, operator recovery untested). The mechanism question is marked explained and its one remaining applicability premise is registered as a gap: whether a node under the captured default snapshot settings (120s interval, 8192 threshold) can actually present a window above the bound at restart. A second, independently sourced lead is recorded as a paused child question on the TimeoutNow authority path — the handler has no term, sender or membership validation and its votes waive the known-leader rejection — with the resume conditions that must hold before it becomes a claim.
